paragraphs: This position paper argues that AI progress should account for the resources needed to achieve a capability. Its motivation is that continually increasing model size and computation can worsen environmental costs and unequal access. The authors propose evaluating development choices through capability per resource and present a theoretical framework for allocating effort accordingly.

The analysis considers transformers in which parameter influence follows a heavy-tailed distribution: a relatively small subset has disproportionately large effects. Under this framework, updating high-influence parameters strictly improves performance per resource over updating every parameter. Gradient norms provide inexpensive indicators of influence, while selecting parameters and training data together yields multiplicative efficiency gains that could reduce resource needs by orders of magnitude.

The proposed workflow pairs pretraining guided by marginal returns with influence-guided adaptation. Gradient blueprints would communicate which parameters matter for different tasks. These are theoretical arguments and a proposed development paradigm; the potential resource savings should be understood within that framing, rather than as reported deployment measurements.
neurips-2025-ai-progress-should-be-measu.tldr: This position paper proposes measuring AI progress by capability per resource and using parameter influence to guide more efficient training and adaptation.

paragraphs: Understanding a chart requires more than reading its labels: a model must also reason about visual information. The authors first study synthetic questions that can only be solved visually. As visual complexity increases, model performance deteriorates substantially while human performance stays robust, motivating a closer examination of this imbalance.

ChartMuseum contains 1,162 expert-annotated questions drawn from real-world charts across 184 sources. Its questions cover multiple reasoning types and combine demanding visual and textual reasoning. This makes it useful for distinguishing models that perform similarly on earlier chart benchmarks where scores are already near saturation.

Humans achieve 93% accuracy, compared with 63.0% for Gemini-2.5-Pro and 38.5% for Qwen2.5-VL-72B-Instruct, the leading open-source model in the evaluation. Every evaluated model shows a reported 35%–55% performance drop on primarily visual questions relative to text-heavy ones. Together with qualitative error analysis, these findings show that strong chart scores can conceal substantial weaknesses in visual reasoning.
neurips-2025-chartmuseum-testing-visual-.tldr: ChartMuseum exposes substantial gaps between human and model chart understanding, especially when questions demand visual reasoning.

paragraphs: Text-to-image models can struggle to place objects according to a prompt, especially in complicated scenes. Providing a layout helps, but planning that layout separately from image synthesis makes it difficult to revise the arrangement as the image develops. CoT-Diff connects those two processes throughout generation.

At each denoising step, a multimodal large language model examines intermediate image predictions and updates a three-dimensional scene layout. The revised layout becomes semantic conditions and depth maps, which enter the diffusion model through a condition-aware attention mechanism. This gives subsequent generation steps both information about scene content and guidance about spatial structure.

The step-by-step reasoning therefore takes place inside a single diffusion round, allowing planning to respond to the developing image. On 3D Scene benchmarks, the authors report improved spatial alignment and compositional fidelity, including a 34.7% improvement over the state-of-the-art method in complex-scene spatial accuracy. These results support tightly coupling layout refinement with synthesis for the evaluated spatial composition tasks.
neurips-2025-cot-lized-diffusion-let-s-r.tldr: CoT-Diff repeatedly revises a 3D scene layout during diffusion to improve how faithfully generated images follow spatial instructions.

paragraphs: Generating sequences of different lengths is natural for autoregressive models, which produce tokens sequentially. Non-autoregressive models often organize generation around fixed token positions, making length changes awkward. Edit Flows addresses this by treating the evolving sequence as something that can be edited, with insertions, deletions, and substitutions as its basic operations.

The model places those operations within a continuous-time Markov chain over possible sequences. Insertions and deletions let sequence length change during generation, while substitutions revise existing content. This supports generation relative to positions in the current sequence. For training, the authors introduce auxiliary variables into an expanded state space, making the learning procedure efficient and tractable.

Experiments show that Edit Flows outperforms both autoregressive and mask-based models on image captioning. For text and code generation, the reported significant advantage is over the mask-based construction. These findings support sequence editing as a useful foundation for flexible non-autoregressive generation, while preserving the distinct comparisons reported for each task.
neurips-2025-edit-flows-variable-length-.tldr: Edit Flows generates variable-length sequences through insertions, deletions, and substitutions within a non-autoregressive discrete flow model.

paragraphs: Instruction-based image editing asks a model to modify an image according to a natural-language request. The paper identifies a precision–efficiency tradeoff: existing fine-tuning approaches can require more than ten million training examples and substantial computation, while training-free approaches struggle to understand instructions. ICEdit seeks to make better use of abilities already present in large diffusion transformers.

Its central contribution is an in-context editing approach that requires no architectural changes. A small amount of parameter-efficient fine-tuning improves quality. The framework also introduces Early Filter Inference-Time Scaling, which uses vision-language models to select high-quality noise samples, making sample selection part of its efficiency strategy during inference.

The authors report state-of-the-art editing performance using only 0.1% of the training data and 1% of the trainable parameters compared with previous methods. These findings support combining an existing model's comprehension and generation abilities with limited adaptation and inference-time selection. The reported resource reductions concern training data and trainable parameters, alongside the demonstrated editing performance.
neurips-2025-enabling-instructional-imag.tldr: ICEdit combines in-context diffusion editing, limited fine-tuning, and noise-sample selection to achieve strong editing performance with far fewer training resources.

paragraphs: Active learning reduces labeling costs by choosing which examples should receive annotations. Good choices depend on both how sensitive the model is to an example and how uncertain its prediction is. For regression, the paper identifies uncertainty as a particular difficulty: estimating it without the true numerical labels is challenging, which can weaken sample selection.

The authors introduce auxiliary data as a source of uncertainty information. Their theoretical analysis shows that such data can provide a useful surrogate even when its distribution differs from the target data, provided it is weighted appropriately. AGBAL implements this idea by recalibrating auxiliary-data losses with density ratio weighting and using the resulting uncertainty estimates to guide selection.

The approach makes imperfect auxiliary information useful through a correction for distribution differences. Across synthetic and real-world datasets, AGBAL consistently outperforms the evaluated methods that do not use auxiliary data. The findings support weighted auxiliary losses as a practical aid to regression active learning, with appropriate weighting central to the theoretical justification.
neurips-2025-enhancing-deep-batch-active.tldr: AGBAL uses appropriately weighted auxiliary-data losses to estimate uncertainty and improve active sample selection for regression.

paragraphs: Video diffusion models can generate coherent content but require substantial inference computation. Lower-precision arithmetic and sparse computation can each help, yet simply combining them without training can damage generation quality. FPSAttention jointly designs FP8 quantization and sparsity around the model's three-dimensional bidirectional attention.

The method uses a common 3D tile structure for both quantization and sparsity, so the two techniques operate at compatible granularity. It also adjusts its strategy across denoising steps because the errors introduced by these approximations are strongly related to the noise schedule. A hardware-oriented kernel combines FlashAttention with optimizations for the Hopper architecture to execute the resulting attention efficiently.

The authors train the approach on Wan2.1 models with 1.3 billion and 14 billion parameters and evaluate it using vBench. At 720p, they report a 7.09-fold attention-kernel speedup and a 4.96-fold end-to-end generation speedup over a BF16 baseline without sacrificing generation quality. The distinction between kernel and full-generation speedups shows how attention acceleration translates into overall gains.
neurips-2025-fpsattention-training-aware.tldr: FPSAttention jointly trains FP8 quantization and sparse attention, delivering a reported 4.96-fold video-generation speedup while preserving quality.

paragraphs: Autoregressive image models produce high-quality images but generate tokens sequentially, making inference slow. Speculative decoding uses a smaller draft model to approximate a larger model's output and offers a possible route to acceleration. Applying it to images is challenging because the sampling space is much larger and image content has an inherently two-dimensional structure.

Hawk uses that spatial structure to guide the speculative model's predictions. The motivation is that nearby image content contains useful local dependencies, but an approach that inadequately uses spatial context misses this information. Better spatial guidance is intended to improve agreement between the draft and target models, addressing a central difficulty in image speculation.

Across multiple text-to-image benchmarks, Hawk achieves a reported 1.71-fold speedup over standard autoregressive models while preserving image fidelity and diversity. The results show that spatially informed speculative prediction can reduce generation time in the evaluated setting. Preserving both reported qualities matters because acceleration should retain image quality as well as variation among generated images.
neurips-2025-hawk-leveraging-spatial-con.tldr: Hawk uses image spatial structure to improve speculative decoding, achieving a reported 1.71-fold speedup while preserving fidelity and diversity.

paragraphs: A multimodal model's key–value cache grows as it processes more video, creating a problem for devices with fixed memory. Existing compression approaches may require the complete video, the user's question, or an already constructed full cache. InfiniPot-V instead compresses during streaming, enforcing a user-set cache memory cap that does not grow with video length.

The framework monitors the cache during video encoding and compresses it when the threshold is reached. Its Temporal-axis Redundancy metric removes tokens that repeat information across time. Value-Norm ranking helps retain semantically significant tokens. Together, these mechanisms select information to preserve without retraining the model or knowing the eventual query.

Tests span four open-source multimodal models and four long-video and streaming benchmarks. The authors report peak GPU memory reductions of up to 94%, real-time generation, and accuracy matching or exceeding full-cache processing, including in multi-turn dialogue. The findings support managing memory continuously as video arrives, making the approach relevant to assistants operating under fixed device-memory constraints.
neurips-2025-infinipot-v-memory-constrai.tldr: InfiniPot-V compresses streaming video caches under a fixed memory cap without retraining or advance knowledge of user queries.

paragraphs: A reward model used in reinforcement learning from human feedback must evaluate responses to prompts it has not previously encountered. The paper argues that training mainly to separate preferred and rejected responses can overlook how the prompt affects those judgments. This neglect may hurt generalization when new prompt–response pairs differ from the training distribution.

The authors separate reward into two independent components. Prompt-free reward depends only on the response, while prompt-related reward reflects the combination of prompt and response. They extract these components using an information-theoretic approach that requires no additional models. Their learning algorithm then prioritizes training examples according to their prompt-free reward values.

Toy examples show that the extracted quantities characterize the two parts of the reward model. Standard evaluations report improvements in both alignment performance and reward-model generalization. The contribution therefore combines a way to analyze what a reward represents with a way to use that analysis during learning, addressing the role of prompts in evaluation.
neurips-2025-information-theoretic-rewar.tldr: This method separates response-only and prompt-dependent rewards, then uses the decomposition to improve reward learning and generalization.

paragraphs: Neural networks can produce excessively large outputs on inputs far from their training data. This paper studies how layer normalization changes that behavior. Using neural tangent kernel theory, the authors analyze infinitely wide networks trained to convergence and prove that including at least one layer normalization operation makes the induced kernel have bounded variance.

Within that theoretical setting, the network's output remains bounded even far from the training examples. The authors also show that a broad class of networks without layer normalization can produce pathologically large outputs for certain inputs. The guarantee concerns output stability under extrapolation; the stated result establishes boundedness rather than correctness on every unfamiliar input.

Experiments on finite-width networks support the theory: a single normalization layer mitigates the uncontrolled growth often observed outside the training domain. The paper also explores protein residue-size prediction for proteins larger than those used in training and facial-age estimation for ethnicities absent from the training set. These applications connect the stability question to concrete distribution shifts.
neurips-2025-just-one-layer-norm-guarant.tldr: For infinitely wide networks trained to convergence, one layer normalization operation guarantees bounded extrapolation outputs, with supporting finite-width experiments.

paragraphs: Some interpretability methods decompose a language model's internal updates into meaningful features, assuming that successive contributions build additively. This paper finds that this picture is insufficient: neighboring transformer layers can systematically counteract each other's updates. The authors call this behavior the Transformer Layer Correction Mechanism.

The mechanism appears in five of seven examined open-source model families and operates across nearly all tokens in varied texts. It emerges during pretraining, is strongest on punctuation and numbers, and adjusts its strength according to the preceding layer's output. The correction targets a small subspace while promoting others, giving it a selective structure.

The authors propose that one layer may introduce several candidate features and the next may reject inappropriate ones. This remains a hypothesis for interpreting the observed behavior. They discuss how the findings help explain vague extracted-feature descriptions, weak steering effects from small feature interventions, and the reported advantage of cross-layer transcoders over sparse autoencoders. The broader implication is that interpreting features may require following their interactions across layers.
neurips-2025-llm-layers-immediately-corr.tldr: Adjacent transformer layers often selectively counteract each other's updates, complicating interpretations that treat features as simply accumulating.

paragraphs: Brain–machine interfaces decode behavior from neural recordings, but those recordings can change substantially over time. Such instability creates a need for frequent decoder recalibration and makes it harder to study neural computations consistently. LINK supplies a long-duration dataset for investigating these changes and comparing methods that handle them.

The dataset pairs intracortical spiking activity with movement measurements from a non-human primate performing a dexterous finger task with two degrees of freedom. It contains 312 recording sessions spanning 1,242 days. This extended coverage directly addresses the stated lack of a standard dataset for evaluating methods over year-long timescales.

The authors also analyze how spiking activity and its relationship to movement evolve, and examine decoding performance using linear and neural-network models. These analyses accompany the publicly available data and code. LINK provides material for work on chronic interfaces, neuroscience methods affected by recording instability, and continuous domain adaptation, where models must contend with changing temporal data distributions.
neurips-2025-long-term-intracortical-neu.tldr: LINK provides 312 sessions of paired neural and finger-movement recordings spanning 1,242 days to study long-term recording instability and decoding.

paragraphs: Language models can struggle when a task requires combining information from many parts of an input. The authors argue that limited capacity for accurate internal communication helps explain these failures. They introduce the bounded attention prefix oracle, or BAPO, as a computational model of bandwidth constraints on attention heads.

Within this framework, some reasoning problems require substantial communication bandwidth. Graph reachability is one example of what the authors call a BAPO-hard problem. Experiments with GPT-4o, Claude, and Gemini align with the theoretical predictions: the models succeed on BAPO-easy tasks but fail on even relatively small instances of BAPO-hard tasks.

The framework also offers an explanation for a benefit of chain-of-thought reasoning. The authors prove that decomposing a task using chain of thought can turn any BAPO-hard problem into a BAPO-easy one. This is a result within their computational framework, alongside empirical evidence about model behavior. Together, the findings motivate architectures and inference procedures that ease internal communication bottlenecks.
neurips-2025-lost-in-transmission-when-a.tldr: A bandwidth-limited model of attention explains observed global-reasoning failures and formalizes how chain-of-thought decomposition can ease communication demands.

paragraphs: MMaDA brings textual reasoning, multimodal understanding, and text-to-image generation into a unified diffusion model. Its architecture uses a shared probabilistic formulation and a modality-agnostic design, eliminating the need for modality-specific components. The goal is to support different data types through a common modeling and training approach.

The post-training process has two central pieces. Mixed long-chain-of-thought fine-tuning uses a common reasoning format across modalities and prepares the model for reinforcement learning. UniGRPO, a policy-gradient algorithm tailored to diffusion foundation models, then combines varied reward modeling to train reasoning and generation within the same framework.

In experiments, MMaDA-8B outperforms LLaMA-3-7B and Qwen2-7B on textual reasoning, Show-o and SEED-X on multimodal understanding, and SDXL and Janus on text-to-image generation. These task-specific comparisons support the authors' claim of strong generalization across the evaluated domains. The work contributes a unified architecture together with a coordinated post-training procedure, and the authors release both code and trained models.
neurips-2025-mmada-multimodal-large-diff.tldr: MMaDA unifies text reasoning, multimodal understanding, and image generation through a shared diffusion architecture and coordinated reasoning and reinforcement-learning training.

paragraphs: This paper examines when accurate learning necessarily leaves identifiable traces of its training examples. It studies stochastic convex optimization under ℓp geometries and calls a learner m-traceable when analyzing its output can identify at least m training samples. The central question connects prediction quality, measured through excess risk, to this form of information exposure.

For every finite p at least one, the authors establish an excess-risk threshold below which every sample-efficient learner is traceable to a constant fraction of its training set. The sample-efficiency condition and the threshold are essential parts of the statement: the result concerns learners operating in that regime.

For p between one and two, the threshold matches the best excess risk achievable by differentially private algorithms, giving a sharp transition with non-traceable algorithms above it. For p greater than two, the result supplies new lower bounds for private learning and partially resolves an open problem. The proof also develops a sparse fingerprinting lemma as a separate theoretical contribution.
neurips-2025-on-traceability-in-ell-p-st.tldr: The paper identifies accuracy thresholds below which sample-efficient convex optimization necessarily exposes a constant fraction of training samples.

paragraphs: Generating gestures from speech requires coordinating the face, body, hands, and overall movement. These components do not all move on the same timescale, and expressive gestures can span different numbers of frames. The paper argues that gesture tokens with fixed frame counts fail to capture these varied patterns across body parts and time.

PyraMotion addresses this with an Attentive Pyramidal VQ-VAE, a model designed to capture motion features adaptively at multiple scales. Its pyramid structure draws inspiration from multiscale visual feature extraction. Attention maps support adaptive integration, allowing information from different temporal scales to contribute to the resulting motion representation.

Objective measurements and subjective evaluations show that PyraMotion produces more natural and expressive full-body gestures than the state-of-the-art methods evaluated. Ablation experiments further identify adaptive integration through attention maps as a contributor to performance. The results support representing gesture patterns at multiple durations when generating coordinated movements from audio, instead of forcing all relevant motion information into one fixed temporal scale.
neurips-2025-pyramotion-attentional-pyra.tldr: PyraMotion adaptively combines motion features across temporal scales to generate more natural and expressive full-body gestures from audio.

paragraphs: Emergency traffic management requires cooperation among traffic lights, emergency vehicles, and ordinary vehicles. The paper argues that focusing only on signal control leaves delays unresolved because vehicle navigation also matters. RMTC treats these components as participants whose roles and policies should adapt to their changing relationships with emergency vehicles.

A heterogeneous temporal traffic graph represents spatial and temporal relationships among the different traffic components at each step. A dynamic role-learning model uses that graph to infer evolving roles for traffic lights and regular vehicles. Multi-agent reinforcement learning then learns traffic policies conditioned on those roles, connecting the current traffic situation to coordinated behavior.

Across four public traffic scenarios, RMTC significantly reduces emergency-vehicle travel time compared with existing traffic-light control methods while effectively preserving ordinary traffic efficiency. This joint outcome matters because the objective includes efficient passage for both groups. The findings support combining relational traffic representations, changing roles, and learned policies to coordinate emergency response across the evaluated scenarios.
neurips-2025-role-aware-multi-agent-rein.tldr: RMTC learns changing roles for traffic lights and vehicles to shorten emergency trips while preserving regular traffic efficiency.

paragraphs: Representation learning can place data in geometric spaces with structures different from ordinary Euclidean space. Hyperbolic spaces and manifolds of symmetric positive definite matrices are established examples. This paper develops discriminative neural networks on Siegel spaces, a family of Riemannian symmetric spaces that has received relatively little attention in machine learning.

The main construction supplies multiclass logistic regression and fully connected layers for these networks. Those layers provide core components for classification directly within the chosen geometry. The approach uses the quotient structure of Siegel spaces and vector-valued distance on Riemannian symmetric spaces, making the geometry part of how the network layers are defined.

The authors evaluate the resulting networks on radar signal classification and node classification. They report state-of-the-art performance across all datasets in their evaluation. These findings demonstrate the relevance of the proposed constructions in two application areas. The contribution is both mathematical and practical: it develops classification machinery for an underexplored geometric family and tests that machinery on classification tasks.
neurips-2025-siegel-neural-networks-0873.tldr: The paper constructs classification layers for Siegel-space neural networks and reports state-of-the-art results on evaluated radar and node-classification datasets.

paragraphs: Arctic sea-ice concentration changes across multiple timescales, but forecasting models often target one temporal granularity. The paper argues that this leaves useful relationships between timescales underused. Short-term fluctuations can accumulate into longer-term changes, while longer-term trends can provide context that helps forecast shorter-term behavior.

SIFusion builds a unified forecasting approach around temporal granularities derived from sea-ice reanalysis data. It combines information within each granularity with information shared across granularities. The aim is to learn representations that remain consistent across timescales, so forecasts can benefit from both local temporal patterns and their relationship to broader trends.

Extensive experiments show that SIFusion outperforms off-the-shelf deep-learning models at the temporal granularities those models specifically target. The stated findings therefore support joint multigranularity modeling for sea-ice forecasting. The approach matters because it treats the connection between short- and long-term behavior as useful predictive information, making temporal consistency an explicit part of the forecasting framework.
neurips-2025-sifusion-a-unified-fusion-f.tldr: SIFusion combines sea-ice information across temporal granularities to improve forecasts by exploiting relationships between short- and long-term behavior.

paragraphs: Checking each step of a language model's reasoning usually requires costly step-level supervision. Self-Play Critic develops an evaluator through adversarial games without manual step annotations. Two copies of a base model take opposing roles: a generator creates deliberately flawed reasoning steps that are hard to detect, and a critic tries to identify the errors.

Reinforcement learning updates both participants using the game outcomes. The winner receives a positive reward and the loser a negative one, driving iterative improvement. This creates a training interaction in which the generator challenges the critic's current ability, while the critic learns to recognize deceptive errors in reasoning.

On ProcessBench, PRM800K, and DeltaBench, SPC progressively improves error detection and exceeds strong baselines, including a distilled R1 model. ProcessBench accuracy rises from 70.8% to 77.7%. SPC also guides test-time search for diverse language models, improving mathematical reasoning on MATH500 and AIME2024 beyond search guided by the evaluated state-of-the-art process reward models. The findings connect better step evaluation with stronger final problem solving.
neurips-2025-spc-evolving-self-play-crit.tldr: SPC trains a reasoning critic through adversarial self-play, improving error detection and mathematical search without manual step-level annotations.

paragraphs: Discrete diffusion models learn distributions over discrete possibilities, but their finite-data estimation error is not well understood. A central difficulty is that the number of possible states can grow exponentially with dimension. An error bound that directly scales with that count can therefore become impractical even when the underlying problem has useful structure.

The paper analyzes error arising from score estimation and uses smooth embedding into continuous Euclidean space to avoid direct dependence on state-space cardinality. This connects the discrete model's structure to properties that can be studied in a continuous setting. The result addresses how accurately a distribution can be reconstructed from limited training data.

The authors establish bounds in two specified settings: a state space organized as a hypercube graph, and one whose graph Laplacian is asymptotically well approximated by the ordinary continuous-space Laplacian. In these settings, the bounds are independent of the number of states. The structural conditions are central to the contribution and explain how the analysis avoids a naive exponential dependence.
neurips-2025-state-size-independent-stat.tldr: The paper derives finite-data error bounds independent of state-space size for discrete diffusion models under specified geometric and graph conditions.

paragraphs: Inference attacks can expose information about a model's training data, including whether a particular example was used. Such attacks often depend on many shadow models, whose independent training is computationally expensive. SHAPOOL reduces this cost by constructing shared models and training them jointly in one process.

The framework uses a mixture-of-experts structure so that different models can share subnetworks. Sharing must still preserve the properties that make separate shadow models useful. Path-choice routing, pathway regularization, and pathway alignment address this through random data allocation for pathway learning, diversity among shared models, and consistency with target models.

The authors evaluate SHAPOOL across several membership inference attacks and report significantly lower shadow-model construction costs with comparable attack performance. The result supports shared training as a substitute for independently constructing every shadow model in the evaluated attacks. The key contribution is making that substitution efficient while explicitly addressing the diversity and target resemblance that sharing could otherwise undermine.
neurips-2025-toward-efficient-inference-.tldr: SHAPOOL shares subnetworks across jointly trained shadow models to reduce membership-inference attack costs while maintaining comparable effectiveness.

paragraphs: Filtering harmful training images assumes that risky content can be recognized in individual samples. This paper studies a weakness in that assumption: a vision-language model may combine information learned from small, benign-looking patches distributed across different samples. The authors call this ability visual stitching when shared textual descriptions connect the fragments.

They first investigate the ability using three datasets in which each image has a unique synthetic identifier. Images are divided into patches at different granularities, and the patch–identifier pairs are used for fine-tuning. Common open-source models can subsequently produce the correct identifier from a complete image or a textual reference, demonstrating integration across the scattered training examples.

The authors then simulate data poisoning with patches from dangerous images and descriptions such as safe or unsafe. The experiment demonstrates how fragmented harmful content can escape patch-level moderation yet later influence responses through visual stitching. The finding identifies a training-data moderation risk arising from relationships across examples, including cases where a model associates harmful scenes with an inappropriate description.
neurips-2025-vlms-can-aggregate-scattere.tldr: Vision-language models can combine scattered training patches through shared descriptions, enabling harmful associations to survive sample-level moderation.

paragraphs: State-space models offer computationally efficient feature extraction for point clouds, but converting spatial data into token sequences can disrupt neighborhood relationships. Random masking during self-supervised training can also weaken local semantic connections. ZigzagPointMamba addresses both the ordering of point-cloud tokens and the way tokens are masked for learning.

A zigzag scan orders tokens globally while preserving proximity between spatially adjacent tokens, improving spatial continuity. The Semantic-Siamese Masking Strategy masks semantically similar tokens and supports reconstruction by integrating local features from original and similar tokens. This is intended to reduce dependence on isolated local features and strengthen global semantic modeling.

The pretrained model improves downstream part segmentation and classification. The authors report a 1.59% mIoU gain on ShapeNetPart, 0.4% higher ModelNet40 accuracy, and accuracy gains of 0.19%, 1.22%, and 0.72% on three ScanObjectNN subsets. These results support considering spatial ordering and semantic masking together when learning point-cloud representations, with benefits demonstrated across the evaluated segmentation and classification tasks.
neurips-2025-zigzagpointmamba-spatial-se.tldr: ZigzagPointMamba combines spatially coherent token ordering with semantic masking to improve learned point-cloud representations.
